observation_summary: FastDateFormat caches instances using a key that inconsistently includes the locale. When the locale is null, it is omitted from the cache key, causing subsequent calls with different default locales to return cached instances created with the wrong (previous) default locale.
reasoning_summary: The bug is in the cache key generation algorithm. The original implementation conditionally added the locale to the key only if it was non-null, but the cached object was created using the default locale if the input was null. This mismatch in the caching strategy (the algorithm for identifying unique instances) meant that the cache key did not correctly represent the state of the object being cached. The fix involves standardizing the key generation to always include the locale (defaulting it if necessary), which is a correction to the procedural logic of the caching mechanism.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'The FastDateFormat getDateInstance() and getDateTimeInstance() methods create the HashMap key from various items including the locale. If the locale is null, then it is not made part of the key... If the Locale is changed subsequently, then the wrong locale is applied.'
The fix_diff_oracle shows that the logic for constructing the 'key' was changed to always include the locale, ensuring the cache key correctly reflects the locale used to create the instance.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves assigning a default locale to a variable, the root cause is the flawed logic of the caching algorithm (the key generation strategy), not just an incorrect initialization.
The fix involves changing conditional logic, but the primary issue is the design of the cache key algorithm, not a missing guard or validation check.
